messages:
aya: Quick update — brought up beryl-int6 on staging and saw a weird recall@1 drop for longtail queries (~4% absolute). posting numbers and a tiny repro.

maddie: oh no, which dataset / slice?

aya: run was on longtail-qa-v2 (same holdout we've used). aggregate recall@1 went from 0.684 (fp16) -> 0.643 (int6). recall@10 mostly stable.

sam: that smells like short-sequence / low-entropy queries getting pushed to wrong neighbors. did you check normalization / L2?

aya: yup — cosine L2-normalized embeddings. distributions look similar overall but sample-level mismatches exist. attached quick UMAP + k-NN diffs.

aya: paste of quick eval command I ran:
```
./eval_embeddings --model beryl-int6 --dataset longtail-qa-v2 --k 1,5,10 --metrics recall,ndcg --normalize l2 --save outputs/beryl-int6.json
```

maddie: can you dump some failing examples? short queries + top2 neighbors for both fp16 vs int6 would be helpful.

aya: grabbing 20 examples now. sending one inline: 
- query: "reset password" (very short)
- fp16 top1: doc_432 (correct)
- int6 top1: doc_17 (irrelevant)
- cosine(fp16,int6) between query embeds: 0.87
- cosine(query_int6, doc_432_int6): 0.61

sam: interesting — inter-model cosine for same item is high but relative ranking shifts. could be quant clamp / bias on specific dims.

aya: ran a quick ablation toggling out per-channel quantization -> per-tensor, and recall@1 recovered to 0.678. so PCB vs PT seems implicated.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary for beryl-int6-per-tensor rolled out to staging at 6141592680 :rocket:

maddie: nice, good catch. can you also check batchsize / kvcache ordering? sometimes microbatching changes activation distribution and quant rounding.

aya: good call — re-ran with microbatch=1 and microbatch=8, negligible diff. kvcache not used for these single-vector forwards.

sam: next steps I'd propose: 1) produce per-dim histograms for fp16 vs int6 for failing queries 2) run per-tensor vs per-channel profile on full holdout 3) try symmetric vs asymmetric rounding.

aya: starting histograms now. throwing a tiny script here for reproducibility: 
```
python tools/quant_probe.py --model beryl --quant int6 --slice longtail-qa-v2 --dump-per-dim=./tmp/beryl_int6_hist.npz
```

maddie: if it's per-channel causing weird scale on low-variance dims we should add a short-term mitigation: prefer per-tensor quant for short queries in routing policy till we understand. can you add a config change PR?

aya: filing PR for a routing override + CI job to run the per-tensor canary. pinging @maddie for review.

ci-bot: [ci] New PR #4624 opened by aya: "routing: prefer per-tensor for shortseq canary" — tests queued.

sam: also curious if this affects embedding clustering (UMAP scatter). if per-channel pushes certain dims to extremes, clusters may fragment. can you attach before/after screenshots?

aya: will attach. early glance: per-tensor looks more consistent with fp16 embedding neighborhoods.

maddie: great. keep the thread updated as PR CI and the per-tensor canary results land. :thumbsup:

aya: thanks — will post results in ~30m.
